Title: Pahang Ruler: Not every Orang Asli land claim is 'customary land'
Article:
ROMPIN: The Sultan of Pahang has called for greater clarity on the use of the term 'customary land' (tanah adat), saying Orang Asli land claims must be assessed according to the legal status of the land.
Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah said the Orang Asli community must not be misled into believing that every area they claim as 'customary land' automatically belongs to them.
He said the matter must be clarified to prevent confusion among the public regarding the Aboriginal Peoples Act 1954 (Act 134) in Peninsular Malaysia, particularly in Pahang.
"Under the Act, there is no specific category known as 'customary land'. Instead, Act 134 provides for the term 'Orang Asli area' (kawasan Orang Asli) under Section 6 and 'Orang Asli reserve' (Rizab Orang Asli) under Section 7, which may be declared by the state authority through official gazettement.
"Therefore, we should not arbitrarily use the term 'customary land' as though every area that has previously been occupied, entered or used automatically becomes a legal right," he said in his speech at the Kenduri Rakyat programme in conjunction with the 2026 Orang Asli Day celebration at Kampung Orang Asli Sungai Mok here today.
Al-Sultan Abdullah said he raised the issue because Pahang has faced numerous land disputes and encroachment cases, some of which have affected public perceptions of the palace and the state government.
He said the Pahang government had never intended to betray or deny the rights of the Orang Asli, adding that their welfare must be respected, preserved and protected in accordance with the law.
"The Constitution itself allows for special provisions for the protection, well-being and advancement of the Orang Asli, including the reservation of land. However, the rights must operate within the framework of the law.
"Under Act 134, the state authority has the power to grant rights of occupation over specific land within an Orang Asli area or reserve. A land claim cannot be accepted merely because an area is referred to as 'customary land'," he said.
He said the status of the land, gazettement, boundaries, history of occupation and facts on the ground must first be examined in accordance with the law before any land claim is considered.
Meanwhile, the Ruler urged that the processes of surveying, marking boundaries and gazetting Orang Asli areas be expedited.
"Clear boundaries are vital to ensure that areas allocated to the Orang Asli are genuinely protected, while at the same time preventing overlapping claims and uncontrolled expansion.
"Individuals or organisations should not mislead the Orang Asli community by creating the impression that every area they claim as 'customary land' automatically becomes their right.
"There are conflicts among the Orang Asli themselves when large-scale encroachment is carried out extensively together with 'towkays' (bosses), using women and children as a means to defend their actions. This must stop... I do not want incidents in Jemeri (Kampung Jemeri, Rompin) and Sungai Cot (Maran) to occur elsewhere," he said.
Meanwhile, Al-Sultan Abdullah said Pahang now has 264 Orang Asli villages, including 30 villages that have been gazetted, while land ownership has been granted to 16 villages.
He said the land status of 46 villages had been settled, while the remaining 218 included 75 applications that were being processed and 31 completed applications awaiting consideration by the State Executive Council.
"Forty-four applications have land overlaps, including those involving permanent forest reserves, Malay Reserve Land and privately owned land. These cases require resolution in accordance with the law and the respective land status.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Three Nepalese workers rescued from burning shoplot
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: Three Nepalese workers were rescued after becoming trapped on the roof of a burning two-storey shophouse this morning.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations John Sagun Francis said firefighters rescued the trio at 7.19am after they became trapped on the second-floor roof and awning.
"Firefighters immediately carried out rescue and firefighting operations, and all three victims were successfully brought to safety," he said.
The fire, reported at 7.01am along Jalan Pasar, involved two adjoining two-storey shophouses.
The blaze was brought under control at 7.15am and completely extinguished at 7.42am.
Firefighters then carried out overhaul work to ensure there were no remaining hazards.
The 42-year-old premises owner was also unharmed.
Eleven firefighters from the Bukit Mertajam and Bandar Perda fire and rescue stations were involved in the operation, which ended at 10.13am.
The case was subsequently handed over to the department's Fire Investigation Division for further action.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thai police charge pub owner as Bangkok fire death toll hit 41
Article:
BANGKOK: Thai police said on Tuesday they submitted charges against the owner of a Bangkok pub to prosecutors, a month after a fire at the venue killed more than 40 people in the country's deadliest blaze in five years.
The charges include negligence causing death, negligence causing serious injury to others, negligence causing physical and mental harm to others, negligence causing a fire, and operating an entertainment venue without a license, Police Major General Kiatikul Sonthinern, the district police commander, told Reuters.
"The owner, however, was still being treated in hospital and was unable to acknowledge the charges," Kiatikul said.
The death toll rose to 41 with 10 in hospital, according to the Bangkok Emergency Medical Centre.
The fire broke out at the Rong Beer Na Lat Phrao pub in Bangkok's northern Chatuchak district after an electrical short circuit caused by unauthorised modifications to the electrical system, he added.
Experts had said non-fire-retardant foam and plastic decor produced extreme heat and toxic smoke, Reuters reported.
The government has vowed to tighten regulations, including random inspections at entertainment venues to ensure safety.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Media industry moves to develop unified audience measurement framework
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian media industry is developing a unified Single Audience Measurement (SAM) framework to tackle longstanding issues caused by fragmented audience data.
Communications and Multimedia Content Forum of Malaysia (CMCF) chairman Datuk Rafiq Razali said the framework aims to provide a single, de-duplicated view of consumers across television, radio, digital media, streaming, social networks and mobile applications, reflecting modern media consumption habits.
This means the same audience is not counted more than once across different platforms.
The initiative, which brings together broadcasters, advertisers, media agencies, digital platforms and streaming services, is spearheaded by the CMCF through a Joint Industry Committee (JIC).
"The media industry cannot make tomorrow's decisions using a fragmented picture of today's audience.
"Malaysians already move seamlessly across television, streaming, social media and multiple devices, but our measurement systems have not kept pace. Through CMCF and the Joint Industry Committee, we are bringing the industry together to close that gap.
"The objective is bigger than creating another dataset.
"We want to establish a common currency that the market can trust when making decisions about content, advertising and investment," he said in a press release today.
Media Specialists Association president Sheila Shanmugam meanwhile said a credible SAM framework would give advertisers a clearer view of audience reach and enable better decision-making.
"One of the biggest challenges for agencies today is that we are often comparing different datasets that were never designed to speak to each other.
"That makes it harder to know whether we are reaching more people or simply reaching the same people across several platforms.
"A credible SAM framework could give advertisers a much clearer view of incremental reach and help us make better decisions about where each ringgit is working hardest," she said.
As part of the initiative, the JIC has issued an industry-driven Request for Information inviting research firms and measurement providers to share global SAM models, methodologies and best practices.
The fact-finding exercise does not commit the industry to appointing any specific vendor. Submissions are open until Sept 14 via www.contentforum.my (http://www.contentforum.my/).
The CMCF is an industry-led forum designated under the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 and registered with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pakistan top court orders ex-PM Imran Khan be moved to hospital from jail
Article:
ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court of Pakistan ordered on Tuesday that former Prime Minister Imran Khan be moved to hospital from jail, his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party said, meeting a longstanding demand of his party and family, who had raised concerns about his health.
Cricketer-turned-politician Khan, 73, has been in jail since August 2023, convicted in a string of cases that he says were politically driven following his ouster in 2022.
His sons repeatedly expressed concern regarding his deteriorating health last year, with his lawyers saying he had lost significant vision in his right eye while in prison.
"It's a very welcome order and we wish it had happened sooner so his eye and general health would not have deteriorated this much," PTI spokesperson Zulfikar Bukhari said.
"He should remain in hospital until all doctors are satisfied," he said.
The court has directed Khan be moved to Shifa International Hospital within 48 hours and remain there until September 16, Khan's spokesperson Naeem Haider Panjutha said on X.
Since he lost power in a no-confidence vote, Khan has faced multiple cases, including over state gifts and an unlawful marriage.
Some convictions have been suspended or overturned, with appeals pending. He denies wrongdoing.
Cricket greats from around the world, including from across the border in India, demanded better treatment for him in February, expressing "deep concern" about his prison conditions.
PTI won power in 2018 and retains a large support base across key provinces.
But it was stripped of its election symbol ahead of the 2024 vote, forcing its candidates to run as independents.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kundasang disaster risk: Fed, state govts must work together, says Kurup
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The federal and Sabah governments must work together to mitigate impacts that could exacerbate disaster risks in Kundasang.
Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES) Minister Datuk Arthur Joseph Kurup acknowledged that the risks associated with natural causes and climate change in Kundasang had increased over the years.
"We have to balance our conservation with our development needs. I have read the reports by the Sabah Works Minister that about 90 per cent of buildings in the area do not have an occupation certificate (OC).
"Under my ministry, we have the Minerals and Geoscience Department, which could monitor all the tectonic activities and slope movements that could give warning to the state.
"But we also need to coordinate with the state to ensure all the buildings built there comply with the safety standards," he told reporters after launching the International Conference on Tropical Forestry 2026 at a hotel here.
Kurup, who is the Nabawan assemblyman and Pensiangan member of parliament, was asked about the ministry's mitigation efforts following the NST's recent special report, titled "
Kundasang's beauty
under threat."
In its recent studies, the Sabah Minerals and Geoscience Department found that a combination of human activities, climate change and earthquakes was taking a toll on the terrain of Kundasang, dubbed the "New Zealand of Sabah."
The department's  report cited  simulation models showing that, in a worst-case scenario, debris flows in the Mesilou catchment area could reach depths of about 25 metres before depositing sediment near populated areas downstream.
On the possibility of using funds  from the proposed National Adaptation Fund for mitigation measures in Kundasang, Kurup said he hoped it could subsequently be used to expand early warning systems, geospatial monitoring and satellite surveillance in areas at risk of natural hazards, including Kundasang.
The fund, which would come from a carbon tax on the cement, energy and steel sectors, is aimed at financing measures to address climate change, including conservation, tree planting, research and development, flood mitigation, slope works and geospatial initiatives.
"The carbon tax is actually under the Finance Ministry, which has the power to collect tax revenue. We (NRES) can only introduce the policy and the framework.
"But I am really trying my best in order to make sure that any carbon tax that we collect goes into this fund so that the people can see where their tax money goes.
"We can also use that fund to help areas such as Kundasang by increasing more early warning systems, as well as geospatial and satellite monitoring. It will also help to improve coordination with agencies such as the National Disaster Management Agency," he said, adding that the carbon tax would only be introduced after the necessary institutional framework was established.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Probe into Malaysia Airlines pilot focused on possible organised crime links
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The police probe into the Malaysia Airlines pilot accused of smuggling drugs into Indonesia is focused on determining whether the suspect is linked to organised crime syndicates.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said this when asked for an update on the case.
He said he received regular updates from Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan, and was inclined to allow the department to complete its probe first.
Saifuddin said the pilot, a Malaysian, was arrested by Indonesian authorities and was therefore subject to the republic's laws.
He said the immediate focus was to extract as much information as possible from the suspect to map out operational patterns.
"We need to establish whether this is part of organised crime or an isolated individual act. We must verify all these facts before deciding on our next move," he said.
On July 28, the 39-year-old Malaysian pilot was arrested at
Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Jakarta
after authorities seized 15 packets containing about 70,000 capsules of ecstasy and methamphetamine, weighing about 25kg and estimated to be worth RM45 million.
Indonesian police revealed that the pilot had been promised RM50,000 to act as a courier for the shipment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: FGV names Nurul Muhaniza group MD, first woman to lead company
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: FGV Holdings Bhd has appointed Nurul Muhaniza Hanafi as its group managing director, effective today, making her the first woman to lead the company.
The company said Muhaniza has been serving as chairman of its board executive committee (BEC) since March.
In that role, she assumed the functions and responsibilities of the group chief executive officer, providing executive leadership and overseeing FGV's operations, strategic priorities and key transformation initiatives.
"Appointed to the FGV board on April 1, 2024, as an independent non-executive director, Muhaniza served as chairman of the board governance & risk management committee and as a member of the board nomination and remuneration committee and board audit committee," FGV said in a statement.
Muhaniza is currently a director of MSM Malaysia Holdings Bhd, where she chairs the investment and tender committee and sits on the audit, governance and risk committee and board sustainability committee.
She is also chairman of FGV IFFCO Sdn Bhd and a director of Cadbury Confectionery Malaysia Sdn Bhd and Nilai Education Sdn Bhd, as well as a member of the board of governors of Nilai University.
Muhaniza holds a Bachelor of Laws from the International Islamic University Malaysia and was admitted as an advocate and solicitor of the High Court of Malaya.
Her career includes serving as an elected member of the Kuala Lumpur Bar Committee, holding key positions within the Selangor State Bar and serving as president of the Strata Management Tribunal under the Housing and Local Government Ministry from 2016 to 2018.
FGV said her experience across the legal, public and corporate sectors had given her broad exposure to legal and regulatory matters, corporate governance, organisational leadership and stakeholder engagement.
"Since assuming executive leadership responsibilities as chairman of the BEC in March this year, Muhaniza has demonstrated steady leadership, sound judgement and clear strategic direction.
"Her appointment as the first woman to lead FGV marks a significant milestone in the group's history, reflecting the board's commitment to recognising leadership based on merit and capability while fostering greater diversity and inclusion," FGV chairman Datuk Abu Huraira Abu Yazid said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Woman, security guard held after Malaysian, Johor flags flown upside down
Article:
KULAI: Police have arrested a Malaysian woman and a Nepali security guard after the Malaysian and Johor flags were flown upside down at a factory in the Indahpura industrial area.
Kulai police chief Assistant Commissioner Tan Seng Lee said the two, aged 34 and 48, were picked up yesterday morning after pictures of the inverted flags went viral on social media.
Both suspects have been remanded for four days until Aug 21 to assist in investigations under Section 5 of the Emblems and Names (Prevention of Improper Use) Act, Section 14 of the Minor Offences Act, Section 505(b) of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act.
The offences relate to the improper use of national emblems, behaviour likely to provoke a breach of peace, actions that cause alarm, and misuse of network facilities. They carry jail terms and fines.
The guard is also being investigated under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act for not having valid travel documents.
Tan said the guard was believed to have put up the flags, while the woman had instructed him to install them.
Images of the flags were initially posted on Facebook and Threads before spreading widely online. The factory was
temporarily shut
after the incident.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MGA targets RM100mil turnover at inaugural Malaysia Gold Festival 2026
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Gold Association (MGA) is targeting RM100 million in turnover from the three-day Malaysia Gold Festival (MGF) 2026, scheduled to be held from Sept 18 to 20 at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre (KLCC).
MGA president Datuk Seri Louis Ng said the target would be driven by a combination of business-to-business (B2B) and business-to-consumer (B2C) sales during the festival. "We do B2B and B2C. B2B sales are very large, while B2C sales may be on a piece-by-piece basis. So, we have a combination of both business entities in this case," he told reporters at the MGF 2026 press conference and official launch of the festival here today.
Ng said MGF 2026 will be the first time the event is being organised on a grand scale, with MGA targeting 70 local and international exhibitors across the gold and jewellery value chain, with about 45 already registered so far. According to Ng, the festival evolved from an initiative that began six years ago. In 2020, MGA introduced the 916 Malaysian Gold Cultural Day, which is celebrated every Sept 16 to recognise Malaysia's gold culture, promote locally crafted gold jewellery and strengthen appreciation for Malaysian craftsmanship.
"The festival is more than an exhibition, as we are taking efforts to encourage Malaysians to support Malaysian gold and invite the world to discover what Malaysia has to offer. Our vision is to establish MGF as a premier annual gold and jewellery event in Southeast Asia, while positioning Malaysia as the region's strategic gold trading and jewellery hub," he said, adding that MGF 2026 is expected to attract between 10,000 and 15,000 local and international visitors.
On the industry outlook, Ng said jewellery demand has started to pick up as gold prices eased from their previous highs, with the recovery also visible in the domestic market. "For the last three to four months (this year), we see demand and sales for jewellery starting to pick up, even in our local market," he noted.
MGA also revealed that it is in the final stage of developing the Malaysia Gold Standard (MGS), the first initiative under the Malaysia Gold Industry Principles (MGIP), to be launched during the festival in September.
He said the MGIP, which comprises eight codes covering various segments of the country's gold industry, including refining, manufacturing, trading and Ar-Rahnu, encompasses the gold industry ecosystem in Malaysia except for mining. Ng said seven codes have been completed, while the eighth, which relates to shariah, requires more time as it represents a new element for the global gold industry.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Duopharma Q2 earnings jump 48pct on better product mix, stronger ringgit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Duopharma Biotech Bhd's net profit jumped 47.8 per cent in the second quarter ended June 30, driven by higher gross profit from a more favourable product mix and a stronger ringgit.
Net profit rose to RM29.86 million from RM20.20 million a year earlier, while revenue increased 5.6 per cent to RM234.35 million from RM221.78 million, according to its Bursa Malaysia filing.
The pharmaceutical company declared an interim dividend of 1.5 sen per share, totalling RM14.43 million, payable on Sept 21.
For the first half of the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026, net profit rose 32.1 per cent to RM60.58 million from RM45.84 million.
Revenue, however, edged down 0.47 per cent to RM482.22 million from RM484.52 million, mainly due to the normalisation of insulin sales to the public sector following a one-off surge in the first half of FY25.
Group chief executive officer Wan Amir-Jeffery Wan Abdul Majid said the company would continue to focus on operational efficiency, cost management and the execution of its strategic priorities.
He said Duopharma would also strengthen its supply chain resilience by diversifying active pharmaceutical ingredient sourcing, managing inventory and working more closely with key suppliers.
"Duopharma Biotech's resilient financial performance comes from a healthy order book, diversified revenue streams and strong participation in the public and private healthcare sector," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: German apartment building permits rise 14pct in June as sector recovers
Article:
FRANKFURT: Permits to build apartments in Germany rose nearly 14 per cent in June from a year earlier, statistics office data showed on Tuesday, as the nation's property industry shows further signs of recovery.
Germany's property sector entered a severe slump in 2022 at the start of the war in Ukraine
Permits, which have been increasing in recent months, are an important indicator of future construction activity
In June, approved permits for apartments totaled 21,600 units, up 2,600 from a year earlier
"To be sure, we are coming from a low level and still are far from where we need to be in Germany," said Verena Hubertz, Germany's minister for housing
Higher interest rates and inflation fears in the wake of unrest in the Middle East have recently dimmed the outlook for the German real estate industry
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US home builder sentiment ticks up in August but remains weak overall
Article:
NEW YORK: US home builder sentiment unexpectedly ticked higher in August, but residential construction firms' confidence remains weak overall, weighed down by economic uncertainty, high mortgage rates and steep building costs aggravated by the US-led war with Iran, a survey showed on Monday.
The National Association of Home Builders/Wells Fargo Housing Market index rose one point to a reading of 35 this month from July's unrevised level of 34. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the index would decline for a third straight month to 33.
A NAHB subindex measuring current sales of single-family homes ticked up to 39, the highest since May, from 37 in July, while measures of future sales and prospective buyer foot traffic were both unchanged.
On a regional basis, sentiment edged up in the Northeast, South and West and was unchanged in the Midwest.
The national index level in August marked the 16th straight month it has remained below 40, the longest such stretch since 2012. Indeed, the index has not breached the 50 level demarking business conditions that builders consider to be positive in more than two years.
"While builder sentiment edged higher in August, builders continue to contend with high construction costs and broader economic uncertainty," NAHB Chairman Bill Owens, a home builder and remodeler from Worthington, Ohio, said in a statement. "Rising gas and diesel prices are pushing up material costs, and spec home building remains weak as many prospective buyers stay on the sidelines."
US gasoline prices - driven higher by disruptions to global energy markets caused by the Iran war - remain above US$4 a gallon on average, about 30 per cent higher than this time last year, according to AAA. Meanwhile, the diesel fuel used widely to power construction vehicles and equipment is averaging US$5.45 a gallon, nearly 50 per cent higher than last August.
The residential real estate market remains in a deep rut, with high mortgage interest rates and limited supply of homes on the market hurting affordability and sales rates.
The contract rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage, the most popular US home loan, ticked lower in the week ended August 7 for the first time since mid-June, the Mortgage Bankers Association reported last week. Still, at 6.77 per cent it remains near the highest in more than a year.
Against that backdrop, builders of new homes are turning to price cuts and other incentives to support sales.
"Our latest builder survey continues to show signs of weakness in the home building market," NAHB chief economist Robert Dietz said. "August marked the 16th straight month that at least 30 per cent of builders reported cutting prices to support demand."
The average price reduction was 6.0 per cent, unchanged from July. Nearly two-thirds of builders offered some form of sales incentive.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Asking prices for UK homes show biggest August fall in eight years
Article:
LONDON: Asking prices for newly listed homes in Britain recorded their biggest August fall since 2018 despite a modest pickup in activity after Prime Minister Andy Burnham took office, property website Rightmove said on Monday.
Average asking prices fell 2.0 per cent in four weeks to August 8, sharper than the 10-year average fall of 1.3 per cent
Summer slowdown and 12-year high number of homes for sale weigh on prices
Asking prices were 1.0 per cent lower than a year earlier, the biggest annual fall since December 2023
London saw the sharpest fall with asking prices down 3.1 per cent annually but prices rise in the north of England
Buyer demand up 5.0 per cent since Burnham became prime minister on July 20 but was 10 per cent lower than a year earlier
The average two-year fixed mortgage rate rose to 5.09 per cent from 4.92 per cent a month earlier.
Rightmove cut its forecast for price growth of 2.0 per cent in 2026 and to flat or a fall of up to 2y.0 per cent with risks seen from geopolitical uncertainty, higher mortgage rates and October's budget
The survey was based on prices of properties put up for sale between July 12 and August 8.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kuala Lumpur luxury home deals send average prices up 52pct: Juwai IQI
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A surge in high-value subsale transactions in Kuala Lumpur has pushed the city's average house price up 52 per cent to RM1.203 million, highlighting growing activity in the luxury segment despite the market remaining largely driven by affordable and mid-market homes.
Juwai IQI co-founder and group chief executive officer Kashif Ansari said properties priced between RM750,001 and RM1 million accounted for six per cent of total subsale transactions in the first half of 2026, while homes priced above RM1 million made up 10 per cent.
"We saw a surprising concentration of high-value subsale transactions in Kuala Lumpur this quarter. Luxury buyers were exceptionally active, snapping up 50 per cent more homes worth RM4 million or above, compared with a year ago," he said.
Kashif said the sharp increase in high-value transactions had a significant impact on Kuala Lumpur's average house price, lifting it to RM1.203 million.
However, he cautioned against using the average price as the sole measure of market performance, as a relatively small number of expensive transactions can significantly skew the figure.
"This is why we also rely on the median price to obtain a more complete picture of the market," he said.
The stronger luxury segment comes as Malaysia's subsale market is poised for further growth in the second half of 2026, supported by resilient economic activity, stable financing conditions and stronger demand in key markets such as Johor.
Kashif expects Malaysia's economy to expand by around five per cent this year, providing a supportive backdrop for the property market without creating significant pressure for monetary tightening.
"That's fast enough to support the housing market without being so fast that Bank Negara Malaysia will have to lift the overnight policy rate (OPR). These stable financing conditions are one of the pillars that support the property market," he said.
Malaysia's economy grew 6.0 per cent in the second quarter of 2026 (Q2 2026), beating the 5.8 per cent advance estimate and accelerating from 5.4 per cent in Q1.
The stronger performance was driven by resilient domestic demand and solid export growth, with all major economic sectors except agriculture expanding during the quarter.
For the first half of 2026, the economy expanded 5.7 per cent, significantly higher than the 4.5 per cent growth recorded in the corresponding period last year.
Bank Negara Malaysia said consumer spending remained a key driver of growth, with sustained increases in retail transactions pointing to continued resilience in household demand.
Ansari said the strength of the economy, coupled with a resilient labour market, should continue to support housing demand.
Malaysia's unemployment rate remained stable at 3.0 per cent in June 2026, with about 517,800 people unemployed, according to the Department of Statistics Malaysia.
Against this backdrop, Ansari expects subsale transaction volumes to continue increasing in the second half of the year, while prices are likely to rise moderately as economic conditions remain supportive and more supply enters the market.
Johor is expected to remain among the country's strongest-performing property markets, with the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) and the approaching launch of the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link providing additional catalysts for demand.
Malaysia's subsale home prices rose nearly three per cent year-on-year in Q2 2026, although Ansari said the national figure masked significant variations across states.
Penang recorded the strongest price growth, with median prices jumping 17.1 per cent to RM480,000, partly reflecting a change in the composition of homes purchased during the quarter.
Kuala Lumpur followed with a 12.8 per cent increase, while Sarawak recorded a 10.3 per cent rise. Johor posted the next-highest growth at 8.3 per cent.
"Prices moved upwards in all but three of the states. They fell in Melaka and dropped marginally in Selangor, while Perak remained steady," he said.
Despite the stronger luxury market in Kuala Lumpur, affordability remains the backbone of Malaysia's subsale market.
Homes priced at RM250,000 and below accounted for nearly a quarter of all purchases, while about seven in 10 transactions involved properties priced at RM500,000 or less.
The RM250,001 to RM500,000 segment emerged as the busiest price category, underscoring continued demand for affordable and mid-market homes despite rising prices in several states.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: West River secures feed-in approval for two Perak hydropower projects
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: West River Bhd's subsidiary Neutron Power Sdn Bhd has secured feed-in approval from the Sustainable Energy Development Authority Malaysia for two small hydropower projects in Perak under the 2026 feed-in tariff (FiT) system.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said the projects are located within Hutan Rizab Bukit Kinta in Ulu Kinta and Hutan Rizab Bukit Tapah in Bidor.
The approval covers the total installed capacity, net export capacity and applicable FiT rate for both projects, with the scheduled FiT commencement date set for Aug 17, 2031.
West River said the approval marked another step in its expansion into renewable energy as the group seeks to diversify its earnings through hydropower projects.
The group views hydropower as a long-term growth area, citing its reliability as a renewable energy source and potential contribution to Malaysia's transition towards a lower-carbon energy mix.
West River said it would proceed with the projects in line with regulatory requirements and development timelines while pursuing other renewable energy opportunities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Euro zone bonds join global selloff, yields hit multi-year highs
Article:
LONDON: Euro zone bond yields hit multi-year highs on Tuesday, joining a global fixed-income selloff, as fading hopes for a swift end to the war in Iran drove oil prices higher and fuelled inflation concerns.
Long-standing concerns about fiscal stability in countries such as France, Japan, the UK and the United States also weighed on global bonds, even as recent soft US data have prompted markets to trim their expectations for rate hikes from the Federal Reserve.
Germany's 10-year yield, the benchmark for the euro zone, was last up three basis points (bps) at 3.2478 per cent, its highest level since May 2011. Bond yields move inversely with prices.
Similar moves were seen in France, and the other more-indebted countries of the euro zone like Spain and Italy, where yields rose even more.
France's 10-year bond yield rose to 4.0954 per cent, its highest since November 2008. That pushed the spread between German and French 10-year yields to 86 bps, its widest since October 2025.
LONG-END WORRIES
Concerns over the fiscal outlook tend to weigh more heavily on longer-dated bonds, where prices are more sensitive to shifts in long-term borrowing, inflation and debt sustainability expectations.
Those concerns have been amplified by fears that a prolonged Iran war could lead governments to ramp up spending to cushion the economic impact of energy supply disruptions from the Middle East, while the deteriorating geopolitical backdrop is also driving higher military expenditure.
"Markets are clearly demanding more compensation for locking up capital for very long periods," said Kjersti Haugland, chief economist at DNB Carnegie.
"Future financing needs, and therefore also the supply of government bonds, are substantial, reflecting ageing, rearmament and a greater need for supply security in a world marked by rising geopolitical conflict and unrest."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia's planned commodity exchange likely to cover palm oil, nickel, coal
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia's planned exchange for "mineral and strategic commodities" will likely include palm oil, nickel and coal, a presidential spokesperson said as the government makes preparations to launch the bourse on Jan 1.
President Prabowo Subianto announced the plan during his 2027 budget proposal speech on Friday, saying that Indonesia's aim was to create its own reference price for many of its key commodities.
The exchange is the latest attempt by Prabowo to leverage the country's vast reserves of natural resources to boost economic growth, after announcing policies in May to centralise commodity exports.
Southeast Asia's biggest economy is the world's largest exporter of palm oil, thermal coal and nickel products and a major supplier of coffee beans, bauxite, tin and copper, among others.
The government is currently ironing out the details on how to implement the plan, including the types of commodities that will be traded on the exchange, presidential spokesperson Prasetyo Hadi told reporters on Monday on the sidelines of Indonesia's Independence Day celebrations.
"Certainly it will cover the commodities that are our primary products, such as CPO (crude palm oil), nickel, and coal," he said.
The Financial Services Authority (OJK) will introduce rules for the bourse by Sept 17, its chief Friderica Widyasari Dewi told reporters.
The OJK rules will include the phased transition of trades into the new exchange, she said on Friday, while a separate presidential decree will be issued to list which commodities will trade on the bourse.
The plans were welcomed by the Indonesian Nickel Miners Association, which has been lobbying for a national mineral exchange.
The announcement was an acknowledgement by the government that Indonesia should no longer be a price taker for commodities it supplied in the largest volumes to global markets, association chairperson Nanan Soekarna said in a statement on Tuesday.
The association said the exchange could provide an alternative reference for buyers and sellers seeking more transparent prices that reflect actual output levels at major production hubs.
"However, we emphasise that the success of this exchange will be determined by the strength of data integrity, the clarity of governance, and the involvement of national miners from day one, not by how quickly features are launched," said Meidy Katrin Lengkey, the association's secretary general.
Indonesia has existing commodity exchanges for palm oil, tin and some other commodities. Tin exports are required to go through the local exchange, but trade at the existing palm oil bourse has so far been limited.

Title: 5.8-magnitude earthquake hits southern Sumatra
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A moderate earthquake measuring 5.8 on the Richter scale struck southern Sumatra, Indonesia, at 2.02pm today.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), in a Facebook post, said the earthquake was centred at 0.8 degrees south and 98.3 degrees east, at a depth of 44km.
The epicentre was about 102km northwest of Siberut, Indonesia.
However, MetMalaysia said there was no tsunami threat to Malaysia.

Title: Malaysia's jewellery trade hits RM12.13bil in 1H 2026 – Matrade
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's total jewellery trade grew 10 per cent to RM12.13 billion in the first half of 2026 (1H 2026), sustaining the industry's strong momentum following a record performance last year.
Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade) deputy chief executive officer (Export Acceleration) S. Jai Shankar said the continued growth reflected the strength of the country's jewellery industry and growing global confidence in Malaysia's trade capabilities.
"In 2025, Malaysia's total jewellery trade surged 22.5 per cent to an unprecedented RM22.46 billion, driven by strong growth across both exports and imports," he said in his speech at the launch of the inaugural Malaysia Gold Festival (MGF) 2026 here, today.
He said jewellery exports rose 9.3 per cent to RM10.1 billion in 2025, with personal ornaments accounting for 85.5 per cent of total exports, reflecting strong international confidence in Malaysian craftsmanship and quality.
Imports soared 35.8 per cent to RM12.3 billion, signalling vibrant domestic consumer demand and Malaysia's increasingly important role within global retail supply networks, he added.
Jai Shankar said the United Arab Emirates (UAE) was Malaysia's largest jewellery export market last year, with exports valued at RM3.4 billion, accounting for 33.9 per cent of total exports.
This was followed by Singapore at RM3.1 billion or 30.2 per cent, Thailand at RM1.1 billion (10.7 per cent), Australia RM0.7 billion (6.8 per cent), and Hong Kong at RM0.6 billion (6.2 per cent).
He said the performance was a testament to the grit of Malaysian manufacturers, the strategic agility of traders and growing international confidence in the country's trade capabilities.
On the industry's strengths, Jai Shankar said Malaysia has a world-class jewellery sector supported by a strong ecosystem of artisans, manufacturers and micro-financing partners.
"The industry, powered by the 916 gold standard, is anchored in Penang and the Klang Valley, which together account for more than 80 per cent of Malaysia's gold jewellery production.
"Malaysia's jewellery industry also combines traditional craftsmanship with modern manufacturing technologies, including 3D engraving, while incorporating Malay heritage, Chinese symbolism, Indian motifs and modern minimalist designs," he said.
He noted that Malaysia has built a strong legacy as a global jewellery exporter and remains a leading player within Asean, with the industry continuing to embrace intelligent manufacturing while preserving its traditional craftsmanship.
The MGF 2026 is the country's first large-scale industry-led gold festival and exhibition, organised by the Malaysia Gold Association.
It is co-organised by the Malaysia Indian Goldsmith Jewellers Association, Persatuan Pajak Gadai Islam Malaysia and Province Wellesley Gold and Silver Ornament Merchants Association, bringing together stakeholders across the gold and precious metals ecosystem under one integrated platform.
MGF 2026, held from Sept 18 to 20, 2026 at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre, features exhibitions, business networking, industry forums, educational programmes, cultural showcases, and public engagement activities.

Title: Penang Customs seizes RM2.53mil in cigarettes, liquor in three raids
Article:
BUTTERWORTH: Penang Customs seized more than one million cigarettes and 18,400 litres of liquor worth RM2.53 million in three raids in Kedah and Penang, and arrested one man.
The seizures were made in Kulim, Kedah, and Bukit Mertajam and Sungai Jawi in Penang between July 10 and July 31.
The contraband was believed to have been stored in residential properties before being distributed locally.
Penang Customs director Hasbollah Din said the operations were mounted based on intelligence received by the department.
"The three cases involved cigarettes and liquor suspected to be uncustomed goods, which were concealed in premises to evade detection by the authorities," he told newsmen here today.
Uncustomed goods refer to goods on which the required customs duties have not been paid.
The biggest haul involved the third case, in which enforcement officers seized 777,400 cigarette sticks worth RM843,827.60, including duties and taxes, from a house in Sungai Jawi on July 31.
A man in his 40s was detained in connection with the raid.
Hasbollah said the first raid, conducted at 2pm on July 10, involved a house in Kulim, Kedah, where officers found 205,880 cigarette sticks and 12,464.20 litres of beer and liquor.
The seizure was valued at RM1.286 million, including duties and taxes, making it the largest of the three cases by total value.
About 90 minutes later, at 3.30pm, officers raided another house in Bukit Mertajam and seized 31,840 cigarette sticks and 5,945.30 litres of beer and liquor worth RM398,449.55.
Hasbollah said all three premises were residential properties and the contraband was found in various parts of the houses.
"The premises were unoccupied when our officers conducted the raids," he added.
Hasbollah said investigations were ongoing to determine who was behind the storage and distribution of the contraband, including how long the premises had been used.
"We are still investigating the cases," he said when asked whether the premises were rented by the same syndicate.
The three cases are being investigated under Section 135(1)(d) of the Customs Act 1967.
A person convicted may be fined 10 to 20 times the value of the goods, but the fine must not be lower than the minimum amount prescribed by law.

Title: Elderly man jailed 13 years for killing friend in care home fight
Article:
MUAR: A 68-year-old man was sentenced to 13 years in jail by the High Court today for causing the death of his friend during an armed fight at an elderly care home in Kluang seven years ago.
Mansur Poh Abdullah pleaded guilty to an alternative charge under Section 304(a) of the Penal Code for culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
Judge Zamri Bakar imposed the sentence on Mansur for causing the death of Asri Asmadi, 55, at the care home in Kampung Chokru, Batu 7, Simpang Renggam, Kluang, at 7.05pm on Oct 10, 2019.
The court heard that police received a call at 8.12pm that a man had died at the care home and subsequently detained Mansur for questioning.
During questioning, Mansur admitted using a parang and scissors during the fight with Asri.
Prior to that, Mansur had told residents not to switch on a rear light as it caused glare. Asri accidentally switched it on, prompting Mansur to become angry and hurl vulgarities at him.
Mansur later went to the kitchen and washed the parang and scissors.
Several residents witnessed the incident, while a care home worker who heard the commotion rushed to the room and found Asri lying in a pool of blood, with Mansur still holding the parang.
Deputy public prosecutor Othman Affan Ismail appeared for the prosecution, while Mansur was represented by lawyers T Amuthen, Chong Chai Ling, S Paul Krishnaraja and S Virochean.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Boost rolls out digital banking, payments platform for SMEs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Axiata Group Bhd's majority-owned Boost Holdings Sdn Bhd has launched Boost SME, a digital platform combining business banking, payments and financing services for small and medium enterprises (SMEs).
The platform allows businesses to open accounts digitally in five minutes, accept payments via DuitNow QR, online payments and cards, and receive same-day DuitNow QR settlements.
Boost group chief executive officer Sheyantha Abeykoon said the platform was developed to make banking, payments and financing more accessible to businesses.
"As Malaysia's digital economy continues to evolve, businesses need financial services that work seamlessly together rather than in silos," he said at the launch today.
Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said the platform could help address the fragmented nature of existing government incentives and financial support available to SMEs.
Under Boost Grow, businesses can earn 3.0 per cent per annum in daily interest on business banking balances, with no lock-in period or minimum balance.
Boost Flow, meanwhile, offers a 0.1 per cent sales rebate on up to RM2,000 in monthly sales for merchants using Boost payment rails.
Eligible merchants can also access a Merchant Cash Advance with credit limits starting from RM10,000, subject to transaction criteria.
Boost SME users can apply for Boost Bank's Biz Loan, which offers financing of up to RM300,000.
The company said loan approvals could take as little as 10 minutes, with disbursement within 24 hours of acceptance.

Title: More Trump-Kim 'love'? What we know about North Korea
Article:
US President Donald Trump says Kim Jong Un had responded to his recent overtures and praised his relationship with the North Korean leader a day after scaling back military drills with South Korea.
Analysts say Kim now enjoys greater global stature, buoyed by crucial backing from Russia and China as well as an improving economy.
AFP looks at what we know about the nuclear-armed country's current state:
Ties with Russia
North Korea has been playing a more active role in international conflict, notably backing Russia in its invasion of Ukraine.
Pyongyang's participation in the war has brought the impoverished country economic and military benefits as well as valuable battlefield experience, analysts say.
Hong Min, a senior researcher at the Korea Institute for National Unification, said North Korea had gained "practical experience across virtually every aspect of modern warfare", including land, air and sea operations, as well as drones.
Last week, Colonel Ryan Donald, spokesman for the US-South Korean Combined Forces Command, said the allies would prepare troops for a potential fight against North Korean forces battle-hardened in Europe.
Showing his elevated status, Kim appeared alongside Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin at a military parade in Beijing last year.
Once 'in love'
Trump met Kim three times during his first term – once declaring they were "in love" – in high-profile summits aimed at securing a denuclearisation deal, but no tangible progress was made.
The US president even bucked decades of US policy by stating North Korea was "sort of a nuclear power" in October.
But Trump's comment at the time – that he was "100 per cent" open to meeting Kim again – have gone unanswered.
Analysts say with Russia's critical backing, Kim now has fewer reasons to engage with Trump.
Kim "no longer needs the legitimacy of a handshake; he needs guaranteed, irreversible sanctions relief before he even walks into the room", Seong-Hyon Lee, a visiting scholar at the Harvard University Asia Center, told AFP.
Missile tests and drills
Pyongyang has also recently bristled at Japan's military build-up, firing ballistic missiles after Tokyo – a key security ally of Washington and Seoul – pledged to strengthen its defences with a "sense of urgency and crisis."
The North has long condemned annual US-South Korea joint exercises as rehearsals for invasion, often staging missile launches around the drills.
During his first term, Trump said after his initial meeting with Kim in Singapore in June 2018 that Washington would suspend the "provocative" drills.
[[nid:1513748]]
The United States stations about 28,500 troops in South Korea to bolster the country's defences, a legacy of the 1950-53 Korean War that ended with an armistice rather than a peace treaty.
Apart from Seoul, other US partners across the region are under pressure to spend more on their militaries, including Taiwan, which Beijing claims is part of its territory and has threatened to use force to annex.
Improved economy
Largely thanks to its participation in Moscow's war against Ukraine, South Korea's central bank estimated last month that Pyongyang's economy grew more than three percent for a third straight year in 2025.
"The expansion of economic cooperation with Russia was a major driver of North Korea's growth last year," a BoK official told AFP.
More weapons exports to Russia boosted related manufacturing, while Russian tourists and expanded transport links lifted construction and services, she added.
China, Washington's chief geopolitical rival, has also been a major North Korean trading partner and a key source of diplomatic and economic support for the country, hit by multiple international sanctions.
Annual bilateral trade – a significant component of which is wigs made in the North – has reportedly recovered since the pandemic to almost US$3 billion.
Seoul the 'enemy'
South Korea's dovish President Lee Jae Myung has pursued engagement with the North since taking office in June 2025, in contrast to his hardline predecessor Yoon Suk Yeol.
But Pyongyang has rejected his overtures, labelling Seoul its "most hostile" enemy and declaring itself an "irreversible" nuclear state.
Seoul has persisted, with its unification minister saying in July it had shifted from prioritising denuclearisation to halting the expansion of Pyongyang's nuclear activities.
Lee proposed talks at the weekend to formally end the Korean War and said Tuesday that joint US-South Korean drills showed no "intention to attack North Korea or escalate tensions on the Korean peninsula."
Park Won-gon, a professor at Ewha Womans University, said Seoul could still play "a constructive supporting role" if US-North Korea talks resume.
But, unlike Trump's first term when inter-Korean ties improved alongside US-North Korea dialogue, Pyongyang could now "bypass" Seoul, he added.
* The writer is from AFP

Title: Home Ministry uses drones to track drug addicts
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The National Anti-Drugs Agency (AADK) has deployed 18 drones to track suspected drug addicts across mapped hotspots, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said today.
​He said the drones provide round-the-clock surveillance to ensure accurate intelligence before enforcement operations are carried out.
"​Data gathered by the drones is sent directly to the operations room, enabling targeted action.
"Through this drone surveillance, a total of 23,317 persons of interest were identified, leading to subsequent arrests of those involved," he said after attending the signing of memorandum of understanding between the Immigration Department and Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission.
He said that the 18 drones enhance AADK's operational capabilities alongside its existing mapping of drug hotspots, which is conducted together with the Narcotics Crime Investigation Department.
Saifuddin said that AADK also launched its strategic plan for 2026 to 2030, which will guide the agency's core operations in prevention, enforcement, treatment, and rehabilitation.
He said the memorandum is to establish a more systematic, effective, and comprehensive partnership.
"​The MOU focuses on four main pillars: capacity building and human resources, intelligence sharing, joint investigations, and joint operational action derived from surveillance findings."
Saifuddin expressed confidence that the strategic collaboration between both enforcement agencies is a step in the right direction.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mother fined RM6,000 for using disabled child's account in rental scam
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: A mother of five was fined RM6,000 by the Sessions court today for using her disabled child's bank account to facilitate a RM1,500 rental scam.
Noor Fazira Sinen, 31, who is married to a policeman, pleaded guilty after the charge was read before Judge Hafizah Abdul Rajak.
The housewife, who is pregnant with her sixth child, broke down in tears while appealing for a lenient sentence, telling the court she was also caring for her elderly mother.
Hafizah fined her RM6,000, in default three months' jail
According to the charge, Noor Fazira used her child's bank account to facilitate a transaction that caused the victim, Anis Amera Zaini, to suffer RM1,500 in losses.
The offence was committed at Jalan Anggerik 2/12, Taman Anggerik Tenggara, Bandar Tenggara, between April 30 and May 22.
She was charged under Section 424A of the Penal Code for unlawful possession of another person's bank account, which carries a fine of between RM5,000 and RM50,000, imprisonment for up to five years, or both upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Inspector Muhammad Husni Abu Hassan appeared for the prosecution, while Noor Fazira was unrepresented.
The court heard that on April 30, the complainant was lured by a Facebook advertisement for a non-existent rental property and transferred RM1,500 into an account belonging to Noor Fazira's child.
The court did not disclose the child's gender.
The complainant became suspicious after failing to receive the promised house keys and subsequently lodged a police report in Bandar Tenggara.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malakoff appoints related party MMC Engineering for RM26.85mil project
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malakoff Corp Bhd's unit Alam Flora Environmental Solutions Sdn Bhd has appointed MMC Engineering Sdn Bhd for RM26.85 million worth of construction works for its Sustainable Facility and Eco-Park Centre in Kemaman, Terengganu.
Malakoff said in a Bursa Malaysia filing today that the contract covers civil, structural, building, infrastructure and utility works, as well as related mechanical and electrical works.
The construction period is 15 months from the commencement date to be stipulated in the definitive contract, with a two-year defects liability period upon completion.
MMC Engineering is a subsidiary of MMC Corp Bhd, a major shareholder of Malakoff, making the appointment a related party transaction under Bursa Malaysia's Main Market listing requirements.
Malakoff said Datuk Mohd Nazrul Izam Mansor, who represents MMC on the boards of Malakoff and Alam Flora Sdn Bhd and is also MMC group chief executive officer, is deemed interested in the contract.
He has abstained and will continue to abstain from all deliberations and voting relating to the contract.
The contract is in the ordinary course of Alam Flora Environmental's business and does not require approval from Malakoff's shareholders or any regulatory authorities.
The applicable percentage ratio for the transaction is 0.60 per cent, exceeding the 0.25 per cent disclosure threshold under the listing requirements.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Elderly far more at risk from rising heat than thought: Study
Article:
PARIS: The threat that rising temperatures fuelled by climate change pose to the health of older people has been dramatically underestimated, according to a US modelling study published Tuesday.
The research was released during a blistering northern hemisphere summer when extreme heat broke numerous records and contributed to the deaths of tens of thousands of people.
For the study, a US team led by researchers at Stanford University sought to estimate how often human-caused global warming will push temperatures to levels that elderly people cannot tolerate.
Previous research in this area has used a measurement called wet-bulb temperature, which incorporates humidity to estimate how much heat a human body can withstand.
However this research was conducted on young, healthy adults, according to the study in The Lancet Planetary Health.
This means it did not take into account the greater risk heat poses to older people because they sweat less and tend to have weaker hearts as well as pre-existing medical conditions.
So the researchers used new data from more recent wet-bulb experiments conducted in the United States which tested how people over 60 tolerated higher heat and humidity.
Taking into account the world's ageing population, they then modelled how heat will affect the health of three different age ranges by 2100 under varying levels of global warming.
"Intolerable heat will be experienced at much larger scales and for longer durations, affecting far more people than previously estimated," the study concluded.
If the world gets 1.5C warmer than pre-industrial levels, 22 per cent of people over 60 will be exposed to unsafe heat for at least a month every year worldwide, the researchers estimated.
Each extra degree of warming will mean a billion more people will experience roughly another month of heat and humidity beyond what their body can tolerate.
If the world warms by 3C, elderly people in the worst-affected regions – south Asia and the Gulf – could face dangerous heat day-and-night for three straight months a year, according to the study.
The countries facing the greatest threat were said to be those with high levels of poverty and little access to cooling, including India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Myanmar and Niger.
"These results suggest that uncompensable heat could increasingly drive internal displacement and transboundary climate migration, raising new policy and humanitarian challenges," the study warned.
To avoid these grim scenarios, the researchers called for the world to cut emissions of planet-warming greenhouse gases – and for future heat plans to prioritise vulnerable older people.
Most deaths from heat happen indoors, meaning that "broader access to air-conditioning and other cooling facilities" is particularly important, they emphasised.
Wildfires, long heatwaves and drought have ravaged Europe during what is expected to be the world's fastest-warming continent's hottest summer on record.
Next year is expected to be even hotter.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hat Yai police deny harassing Malaysian bikers over traffic offences
Article:
KOTA BARU: Hat Yai police have denied harassing or intimidating a group of Malaysian motorcyclists, saying the enforcement action was carried out in accordance with Thai traffic laws.
The clarification came after a Malaysian social media user, known as "Tok Singa", posted a video claiming that his group of 17 Malaysian bikers had been detained by Hat Yai traffic police and issued 15 summonses involving fines totalling 15,000 baht (about RM1,850).
The post, which also alleged that police took almost three hours to conduct checks and threatened to detain the rider if the fine was not paid on time, went viral and prompted calls among Malaysians to avoid travelling to Hat Yai.
Hat Yai Traffic Police chief Police Lieutenant Colonel Weerasak Phunsak said the actual circumstances differed from those portrayed in the viral video.
He said officers spotted the group of about 17 motorcycles while on duty in front of the Hat Yai Police Station and noticed some motorcycles had modified flashing rear lights and noisy exhaust systems.
"We followed the group to the Saphan Dam intersection to conduct safety and regulatory checks before inviting them to the police station for a detailed inspection of their documents, driving licences and motorcycle equipment," he said.
Weerasak said all 17 motorcycles were inspected, with nine found to have committed traffic offences.
He said nine summonses were issued, involving total fines of 12,000 baht (RM1,470), and not 15 summonses totalling 15,000 baht as claimed in the social media post.
"Their offences included using equipment that did not comply with regulations, such as modified flashing rear lights and exhaust systems exceeding permitted noise levels," he added.
He said Thai traffic police also issued summonses for failure to produce a valid driving licence and failure to display proof of coverage under Thailand's Road Traffic Accident Compensation Act.
On driving licences, he said Thai regulations recognised international driving licences or Malaysian driving licence cards bearing photographs issued by the Malaysian Road Transport Department.
He added renewal slips or licences displayed through the RTD application could not be accepted as a substitute.
Regarding exhaust noise, Weerasak said measurements were taken using equipment in accordance with legal requirements.
He said the permitted noise level was based on the vehicle's factory sound level plus five decibels, while vehicles without the required factory measurement were subject to limits based on their registration year.
"Vehicles registered before 2024 are subject to a maximum of 95 decibels, while those registered from Jan 1, 2024 onwards are limited to 90 decibels," he said.
Weerasak said the requirements had been explained to the Malaysian tourists during the inspection.
He claimed the viral video had distorted some of the facts surrounding the incident.
He said that Thai traffic police carried out their duties professionally and in accordance with the law, regardless of whether those involved were foreign tourists or Thai nationals.
"There was no coercion or harassment specifically targeting Malaysians.
"If you are travelling to Thailand for tourism, I urge you to study and strictly comply with the country's traffic laws, even if you are concerned about the impact on tourism.
"However, I believe this incident will not affect tourism in Hat Yai, as most tourists who visit the area strictly follow the law," he said.
It was
reported
yesterday that a trip to Hat Yai, Thailand, for a group of 17 Malaysian motorcyclists turned sour when Thai authorities issued 15 fines totalling 15,000 baht (about RM1,850) for various traffic offences.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cabinet to decide policies for tighter border controls, says MCBA chief
Article:
JOHOR BARU: The Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) will strengthen and better coordinate controls at the country's entry points while ensuring public movement is not unduly hampered.
Its director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain said policy and operational matters relating to MCBA's role would be left to the Cabinet to decide as part of efforts to strengthen border security.
He said the priority was to manage the movement of people efficiently without compromising national security.
"The public must be managed efficiently without compromising national security," he told the New Straits Times after the soft launch of the MCBA office at the Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link Bukit Chagar station here today.
He said MCBA would act in accordance with the policies once they were finalised.
"I don't want to jump the gun. Let the policies be set first, then MCBA will act accordingly," he added.
Earlier, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said a
comprehensive plan
was being drawn up to strengthen controls at the country's entry points following several recent incidents at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA).
This includes the arrest of a Malaysia Airlines pilot in Jakarta for allegedly
smuggling 70,000 ecstasy pills
and methamphetamine into Indonesia, raising concerns over existing security and screening controls at KLIA.
Saifuddin said the plan would be jointly presented with Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook to safeguard Malaysia's image and address concerns over perceived weaknesses in security controls at KLIA.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ex-PM Muhyiddin’s trial: PMO gave names of contractors for Jana Wibawa projects, Finance Ministry officer says
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — The Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) during the Muhyiddin administration had proposed contractors that passed the Finance Ministry’s evaluations and eventually won multi-million ringgit government projects under the Bumiputera contractors’ programme Jana Wibawa, a senior Finance Ministry (MOF) officer told the High Court today.
MOF government procurement division’s secretary Datin Rosni Mohd Yusoff, 54, said this while testifying as the 25th prosecution witness in Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia president and former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s power abuse and money laundering trial.
Rosni today said she chaired an MOF committee that evaluated whether contractors were qualified for Jana Wibawa projects.
This includes these three companies, which other witnesses in the trial had previously confirmed were awarded these multi-million ringgit Jana Wibawa projects:
KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd: Awarded RM62 million contract via direct negotiation to build a new road connecting Felda Bukit Jalor to Gemas, Negeri Sembilan;
Sutracom Sdn Bhd: Awarded RM605.2 million contract via pre-qualification tender to build and upgrade phase three of the Pulau Indah highway in Klang, Selangor;
Nepturis Sdn Bhd: Awarded RM141 million contract via pre-qualification tender to build the Klang Utara district police headquarters (IPD).
Rosni said her committee had evaluated these contractors for Jana Wibawa projects after receiving their names from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), stressing that the committee would not have evaluated these companies if the PMO did not propose them.
For example, Rosni’s committee had evaluated KCJ Engineering after Muhyiddin’s office sent a November 13, 2020 letter to propose the company, and would not have done the evaluation if the letter did not state KCJ Engineering’s name.
“This is because evaluation will only be carried out on companies proposed by the Prime Minister’s Office,” she said today, adding that KCJ Engineering would not have been awarded the project by the Public Works Department (JKR) if it had not gone through the evaluation process.
“Throughout the Jana Wibawa programme, all proposals for names of contractors and projects implemented through direct negotiation were presented by the Prime Minister’s Office. No companies were appointed through direct negotiation without going through proposals from the Prime Minister’s Office and subsequently an evaluation process at MOF,” she said.
Rosni said KCJ Engineering had actually failed the first round of evaluations in December 2020 as it had a “sick” project and unsatisfactory work performance.
But Rosni said her committee had received the PMO’s February 3, 2021 letter containing additional information for several companies including KCJ Engineering in order to re-evaluate the company for the Jana Wibawa project, adding that this PMO letter was received via the Finance Minister’s office.
After receiving this PMO letter, Rosni said her committee held a meeting on February 26, 2021 to evaluate all the KCJ Engineering documents, adding that KCJ Engineering passed this second round of evaluations to be a Jana Wibawa contractor.
Rosni said the committee would not have carried out further action after KCJ Engineering failed the initial evaluation, if her division did not receive any instructions from the Finance Minister’s office based on the PMO’s February 2021 letter.
As for Sutracom and Nepturis, Rosni said her committee would not have carried out any evaluations on whether these two companies were qualified for Jana Wibawa projects, if they had not sent letters through the PMO to express interest in the projects and if the PMO had not forwarded those letters to the Finance Ministry.
“This is because the entire proposal for names of contractors and projects under the Jana Wibawa programme comes from the Prime Minister’s Office,” she said today.
She said her committee had evaluated these two companies as their names were stated in the PMO’s letters to the Finance Ministry in February 2021 and March 2021, pointing out that these companies would not have been eligible to join in the pre-qualification tender for Jana Wibawa programmes if they had not gone through the mandatory contractor evaluation process.
Earlier today, JKR’s former quantity surveyors’ service director Datuk Zulkipeli Yamat as the 24th prosecution witness agreed with Muhyiddin’s lawyer Chetan Jethwani that there was no interference by the PMO when Nepturis was selected to be the contractor for the Klang Utara IPD project.
Zulkipeli also confirmed to Chetan that the PMO was not involved and did not ask for information or follow up during the evaluation of tenders sent by three companies (including Sutracom) for the Pulau Indah project.
Previously, banking evidence and witness testimonies in this trial had shown that money from various companies had entered Bersatu’s bank accounts, including RM1 million from Nepturis and RM800,000 from KCJ Engineering.
Mamfor Sdn Bhd’s managing director Shahradzi Shamsuddin had previously also testified that his company donated RM19.5 million to Bersatu as his younger brother’s company Sutracom was awarded the RM605.2 million project.
In this trial, Muhyiddin is facing seven charges, namely four counts of alleged power abuse to obtain RM225.3 million in bribes for his party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd), and three counts of alleged money laundering involving money that Bersatu received from Bukhary Equity.
The trial before High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin resumes tomorrow.
